items.followUp: Differentiate between RAM and ROM on the basis of data retention.

accept: loses data when power is off
rubric.why: Identifies that volatile memory needs power to retain data.
rubric.description: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is turned off.
rubric.how: Award for stating that volatile memory loses data when power is off.

rubric.why: Identifies that non-volatile memory retains data without power.
rubric.description: Non-volatile memory keeps its data even when the power is turned off.
rubric.how: Award for stating that non-volatile memory retains data without power.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is turned off; RAM is an example.
Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is turned off; ROM is an example.

items.followUp: What is booting, and what happens to the operating system during this process?

rubric.why: Names what is loaded from the hard disk.
rubric.description: The operating system or its system files are read from the hard disk.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the operating system or system files as the data being loaded.

rubric.why: Identifies the destination of the loading process.
rubric.description: The operating system is loaded into RAM (main memory) so the computer can run.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is loaded into RAM or main memory.

modelAnswer: Hard disk loading is the process of loading the operating system or its system files from the hard disk into RAM.
This allows the computer to start and run the operating system.

items.followUp: How does a Caesar cipher encrypt a message?

rubric.why: Identifies the method used by the Caesar cipher.
rubric.description: A Caesar cipher is a substitution cipher that replaces each letter with another letter.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that letters are substituted or replaced.

rubric.why: Identifies the fixed shift applied to the letters.
rubric.description: Each letter is shifted by a fixed number of places in the alphabet.
rubric.how: Award for stating that letters are shifted by a fixed number of places.

modelAnswer: A Caesar cipher is a substitution cipher used to encrypt a message.
Each letter is replaced by a letter a fixed number of places away in the alphabet.

items.followUp: State two advantages of connecting computers in a network.

rubric.why: Gives a key reason for connecting computers in a network.
rubric.description: A network allows users to share resources, such as hardware or files.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning resource, hardware, or file sharing.

rubric.why: Gives another key purpose of a computer network.
rubric.description: A network enables users to communicate and exchange information.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning communication or information exchange.

modelAnswer: A computer network is needed to share resources such as files, printers, and internet connections.
It also allows users to communicate and exchange information.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of HTTP when browsing the web?

rubric.description: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award for giving the correct full form or abbreviation.

rubric.why: Explains the main function of FTP.
rubric.description: FTP is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
rubric.how: Award for stating that FTP transfers files between computers or over a network.

modelAnswer: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.
It is used to upload and download files between computers over a network.

items.followUp: What is meant by a sender in communication?

rubric.why: Identifies what a receiver is in the communication process.
rubric.description: A receiver is the person or device that receives a message.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the receiver as a person or device.

rubric.description: The receiver gets the message sent by the sender.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the receiver receives or gets the message.

modelAnswer: A receiver is the person or device that receives a message.
The message is sent by a sender.

items.followUp: Name two HTML tags that can be used to format text.

rubric.description: Content formatting changes the appearance or style of content on a web page.
rubric.how: Award for stating that formatting changes the appearance, look, or style.

rubric.why: Gives examples of formatting that can be applied to content.
rubric.description: Formatting can make text bold, italic, underlined, or change its size or colour.
rubric.how: Award for giving at least one valid text-formatting example.

modelAnswer: Content formatting in HTML means changing the appearance or style of content on a web page.
For example, text can be made bold, italic, or underlined.
